runners_data.name: If Not For Grace
runners_data.note: OR=120 hold-up filly for Leigh Roche and Liam Cusack who fades in the finish — the hot early pace from the two leaders will not help her get competitive, and just two runs in form with none on this trip suggest she is short of a clear confidence run right now.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, If Not For Grace faces a stiff ask here; 51 days off the track adds a fitness question, though stall two is at least a straightforward draw.

runners_data.name: Contrite
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for the powerful D K Weld stable and that booking always attracts attention; a hold-up operator who placed last time out, Contrite needs the front pair to go genuinely hard so she can mount a late challenge, and the good-to-firm suits her best form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Contrite does bring distance experience and returns on a reasonable 23-day break, but carrying 135 lb from stall 1 and ranked 12th of 18 on ratings, she faces a stiff ask despite a placing last time out.

runners_data.name: Jp's Express
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted apprentice-ridden hold-up type who won over 8f on soft ground recently, so the step up to a mile on good-to-firm is a slight concern; active campaigner with a run just ten days ago, and in an open field could benefit if the front of the race goes haywire.
runners_data.comment: Jp's Express won two starts back but has finished fifth on his most recent outing, and while he has run over today's trip, a mark of 70 and a draw from stall 6 leave him with plenty to find off a solid weight of 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Passage Of Power
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle rides this confirmed front-runner for the powerful Joseph O'Brien yard — OR=120 and two recent runs suggest he is fit and ready; the key question is whether Hello Stacia lets him dictate, and if contested the pace could compromise both.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts, Passage Of Power does bring distance experience to the table and a 35-day break may have freshened him; however, carrying 135 lb from stall 16 while ranked tenth of eighteen on our rating makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Star Of Beauty
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for K J Condon who has posted four placed efforts from nine starts on good ground — the profile of a horse that tucks in just off the pace and stays on, which is exactly the profile this race shape rewards most.
runners_data.comment: Placed three times in her last four starts and back within a sharp 18 days, Star Of Beauty has experience over today's trip and represents a lively threat at a workable weight of 132 lb from stall 18 — though she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Bill Silvers
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type wearing a visor who has struggled to reproduce his best on good ground, finishing out of the frame the last six starts; carrying 129lbs and returning from 34 days off for a stable with no recent form, he is a significant each-way outsider at best.
runners_data.comment: Bill Silvers has run over today's trip and, rated 82 by us against an official mark of 74, holds a clear edge on figures — but he arrives winless in his last five starts, with a pull-up and two unplaced efforts among them, and 34 days off leaves some questions.

runners_data.name: Buttermere Ridge
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who wears a tongue-strap and has a tendency to fade late — the redistribution note reflects that a field this stacked with closers means he will race closer to the pace than he'd like, and his style-fit score of 0.91 flags that out-of-role running is a real concern here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Buttermere Ridge has experience over today's trip and returns quickly on 11 days' rest, but a fourth two starts back represents his best recent effort and he carries 126 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's hold-up operator under Chris Hayes has won once from thirteen starts on good ground, but the redistribution from the rear means he is unlikely to get far enough back; a tongue-strap wearer whose best form at 8f on soft looks a gear change away from this surface.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a pair of fifths two and three runs back offering the best of a modest recent profile, Liberate has run over today's trip and steps out from stall three carrying 126 lb — enough to keep her competitive but her consistency remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Zitkala Sa
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the mount on this lightly-weighted three-year-old hold-up type who wears a tongue-strap — she has been placed once from five runs and, forced closer to the pace by the crowded rear division, her natural finishing move is compromised in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 13 of 18 on our figures, Zitkala Sa is hard to fancy, though a third two starts back offers a slender crumb of comfort from an otherwise disappointing recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Countertop
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted three-year-old who fades in the finish and has struggled badly in recent starts, posting two sixteenth-place finishes; the redistribution note applies and even in a softer race she has not shown enough to be considered a genuine factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Countertop is hard to fancy despite returning quickly seven days after his latest outing; he has run over today's trip before, and the 119 lb burden from stall 12 adds no help.

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who finishes out of the frame regularly on good ground, and the absence of a listed jockey is a flag; headgear of a hood (h) has not unlocked improvement and a run just five days ago suggests connections are looking for a quick confidence-builder rather than a win.
runners_data.comment: Slight Of Foot showed useful form when fourth three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour, with our rating of 72 marking him as a leading threat; the worry is he's been winless in recent starts and returns on just five days' rest.

runners_data.name: Hastily
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who has won once from fifteen starts on good ground and is approaching veteran territory — the redistribution effect is real here, and form figures of 9-0009 confirm how hard he is to place competitively in a field of this quality.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pair of ninth-place finishes the best she can offer, Hastily is hard to fancy ranked 16th of 18 on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 19 days between runs leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Macinamillion
runners_data.note: A 307-day absence is a massive flag for this six-year-old, whose form over extreme trips (18-20f) makes the mile trip a very different test; best form was over much longer distances, and while he has class on paper, the layoff and trip change make him a speculative outsider at best.
runners_data.comment: Macinamillion has been off the track for 307 days and is unplaced in each of his last two starts, which makes him very hard to fancy ranked 14 of 18 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and did win three starts back, but there is precious little else to grab onto here.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: The highest style-fit score (0.94) among the redistributed runners, suggesting Adrian McGuinness's hold-up type handles a range of conditions — two wins from fifteen on good ground and a record of 2W4P in the last five backs this up; if any of the hold-up brigade can make a challenge it is Minaun View, but racing in front of his ideal position is a disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Minaun View arrives on the back of back-to-back wins three and four starts ago, and at just 11 days since her last outing she comes here in peak freshness; she has run over today's trip and carries 128 lb from stall 15, with the seventh last time out the sole caution.

runners_data.name: Hello Stacia
runners_data.note: James Dowling's confirmed front-runner is OR=120 and has placed on both career starts, including a third on this going; ridden by Luke McAteer, she will fight Passage Of Power for the lead and the result of that battle determines whether she lasts or burns out, but a mile on good-to-firm suits her profile if she gets a clean lead.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last two starts, finishing third two starts back before a seventh last time out, Hello Stacia heads into this rated 52 and ranked 15 of 18 — hard to fancy at the weights, though she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Adrian McGuinness under Ronan Whelan who has won once and placed three times from fifteen starts — active recently (run nine days ago) and proven at 8f on good ground, he is well placed to sit just behind the contested pace and mount a challenge in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last six starts, Land Of The Giants does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a nine-day turnaround suggests he's fit; however, inconsistency — with unplaced efforts either side of a third — makes him a tricky proposition from stall five off 127 lb.

runners_data.name: May Night
runners_data.note: An 387-day layoff for this eight-year-old hold-up type with Raymond Hurley is a serious concern — she has some placed form on good ground over a mile but the redistribution effect and such a lengthy absence make a winning run very hard to envisage on return.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after a 387-day absence, May Night faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a third last time out offers some encouragement; our rating of 67 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 52 implies.

runners_data.name: Mythical Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent type wearing a visor for C Byrnes under Sean Davis, with a solid record of three places from eight starts on good ground at this trip — his profile of tracking the pace and staying on is exactly what this race shape rewards, and recent form shows consistency at the level.
runners_data.comment: Ran second last time out and has experience over today's trip, but one of his last five starts has yielded an unplaced finish and he's winless in his last five starts — carrying 127 lb from stall 10 complicates matters further.

races.paceDynamic: Passage Of Power and Hello Stacia are the two confirmed front-runners in an 18-runner field, and both are likely to contest the early lead vigorously from the flag, creating a genuinely contested gallop on good-to-firm ground over a mile at Gowran Park. With two high-rated (OR=120) leaders pushing each other, the pace should be honest rather than suicidal, but it will be enough to stretch the field and compromise those who need a truly strong tempo to deliver their finishing kicks. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the track can accommodate at the rear — Minaun View, Liberate, Buttermere Ridge, Zitkala Sa and others are genuine closers who will be forced wider and closer to the pace than they prefer, diluting the effectiveness of any late surge. This race shape most clearly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the two leaders — Star Of Beauty, Land Of The Giants and Mythical Rock are the profile types best positioned to pounce as the front-runners tire in the final furlong, without being caught in traffic or racing out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Passage Of Power and Hello Stacia share the lead at a strong but controlled pace and the prominent chasers track without incident.
scenarios.body: The two leaders push each other along at a fair clip, burning off the hold-up horses who cannot get far enough back to regroup, while the closest trackers inherit a winning position in the final two furlongs; good-to-firm ground rewards those with tactical cruising speed rather than pure finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pacey Leader Clears Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of Passage Of Power or Hello Stacia breaks cleanly and dominates alone, dictating a more controlled solo tempo.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner who sets an even gallop without being harried can conserve enough energy to last home on the good-to-firm surface, and a prominent runner sitting just off the pace is ideally placed to challenge; with both leaders OR=120, the one who controls the race solo has a genuine winning chance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace between Passage Of Power and Hello Stacia is genuinely fierce enough to set up a strong late run from further back.
scenarios.body: A truly hot pace would compress the leaders and open a window for closers, but this scenario is undermined by the redistribution of most genuine hold-up types who will not be far enough back to benefit fully; Contrite under Colin Keane and Minaun View are best-placed among the hold-up brigade if a proper late run does develop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart — Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace causes interference, the field fans wide, or late market movers exploit a tactical vacuum created by attrition.
scenarios.body: An 18-runner field on a turning track at Gowran creates legitimate traffic risk in the straight, and if the front pair exhaust each other spectacularly, an unexposed or lightly-raced type such as Jp's Express or a revived Macinamillion could steal a race run in chaos.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Passage Of Power or Hello Stacia secures a clear lead at the first bend — if they fight each other hard through the opening quarter mile the pace could become genuinely fierce and collapse both chances, opening the race up for prominent chasers like Star Of Beauty and Land Of The Giants.

Minaun View carries the highest style-fit score among the redistributed hold-up runners and is the one most likely to overcome the out-of-role positioning — monitor market moves for Patrick McGettigan (5) who rides for in-form Adrian McGuinness stable (2/26 over 14 days).

With 18 runners on a turning Gowran mile, early position at the start is critical — hold-up types like Contrite (Colin Keane) and Liberate (Chris Hayes) must avoid being squeezed wide exiting the first turn or their chances of generating a late run are effectively zero.

Star Of Beauty is the most consistent prominent-style runner in the field with four placed efforts from nine starts on good ground at this trip — if the early pace is truly contested she sits in the sweet spot tactically and her visor (v) headgear suggests she is primed to run her race.

The trainer angle for Dylan Browne McMonagle on Passage Of Power is notable — Joseph O'Brien's yard is 7/66 over 14 days, a solid strike rate, and if Passage Of Power can dictate alone he represents the strongest individual case among the front-running pair.

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: Won over this 7f Gowran trip in recent form and returns on just 5 days' rest for Denis Hogan whose 14-day strike rate of 2/33 warrants mild caution; a natural front-runner by instinct who is placed in the mid-prominent zone here because the field is too front-loaded for all of them to lead, so Chris Hayes will need to find a clean position early or face a compromised run.
runners_data.comment: Alfred Tennyson won last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, giving him a solid platform here; carrying 140 lb from stall seven, he looks our pick despite the quick five-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Pretty Omagh Girl
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed leader on a flat 7f track she handles well (1W1P in similar going), returning after 45 days off for A Oliver whose limited recent string (2/6) is manageable; Ben Coen's ability to dictate makes this the race's central pace figure, and the absence of any direct challenger is a significant tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Pretty Omagh Girl won two starts back but has been unplaced on her most recent outing, leaving her form slightly mixed; she has run over today's trip and returns after 45 days off, though she faces a stiff task ranked fifth of seven.

runners_data.name: Indigo Dream
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this 4-year-old who has placed three times in similar going but has a 0W record on turf in this style of race and a form string showing a decline to '7' last time; races prominently but does so without the natural aggression of Alfred Tennyson or Little Empire, and the trip at 7f Gowran is well within range if she rediscovers her earlier-season form.
runners_data.comment: Indigo Dream has shown ability, finishing second twice in recent starts, and she has experience over today's trip, while our rating of 86 ranks her second in this field; the worry is a trainer in poor form at just 3% over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Ohailbhic
runners_data.note: Two wins over further (8f at Sligo) suggest this is a horse stretching to maintain pace over 7f on a flatter track, and the stable's quiet 14-day record (0/4) offers little confidence boost; a genuine hold-up performer who will track from the rear under Ronan Whelan and requires a strongly-run race to get competitive — the controlled pace is not ideal.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins two and three starts back give Ohailbhic some form to point to, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but a seventh last time out and a ranking of seventh of seven on our figures make him hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Lohoobb
runners_data.note: W J Lee picks up the ride on this 3-year-old who has run consistently in similar Good conditions (9/9 in sim-going records) but has never won; by nature a hold-up horse, this runner has been pushed into a midfield position on the map because the rear rank is crowded with similar types, meaning it is unlikely to get its preferred ground-saving position, and the STYLE_FIT flag should discount its prospects accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Lohoobb's claims look slim despite carrying 126 lb from stall 1; he has run over today's trip and going before, but an eighth last time out — just three days ago — makes this a very tough ask.

runners_data.name: Little Empire
runners_data.note: The 6-year-old carries top apprentice claim relief via Patrick McGettigan (5lb) which partially offsets the 139lb burden, and the trainer Anthony McCann has a 1/6 14-day record; prominent by style and consistent in placing at this level (3 places in last 5), Little Empire is well-suited to riding cover behind Pretty Omagh Girl and has the experience to find a clean run in a 7-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Little Empire ran a fine second two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, while his rating of 87 tops this seven-runner field — the main concern is that sixth last time out suggests he can be inconsistent, and he remains yet to score.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's 7-year-old runs in a visor and was placed over 7f Gowran on good recently (3rd) but the form has dipped since (0, 7, 6 in last three); a hold-up performer under Dylan Browne McMonagle who needs proper cover and a clear injection of pace in the final two furlongs to make his effort count — the visor is a fitness/focus aid but the 13-day turnaround is sharp for a horse whose last run reading was a '0'.
runners_data.comment: Exquisite Acclaim showed a promising third three starts back and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround with experience of today's distance and going in his favour — the risk is that he's been winless in recent starts, including an unplaced effort last time.

races.paceDynamic: Pretty Omagh Girl is the confirmed lone pace-setter and will dictate from the front on Good To Firm ground over this flat Gowran 7f, with Ben Coen able to control tempo without any direct challenger threatening to press or burn her. Alfred Tennyson and Little Empire are the natural prominent horses who will push forward behind her, with Indigo Dream also prominent in style, meaning there is legitimate early competition for the positions directly behind the leader but nothing to genuinely destabilise the gallop at the head of affairs. Hold-up types Ohailbhic, Exquisite Acclaim and the redistributed Lohoobb will track from mid-to-rear, relying on a strong finish to peel off the leader's honest pace. This shape strongly favours a horse that can travel prominently, conserve energy behind a controlled solo leader, and deploy a sustained finishing effort in the final two furlongs — the hold-up contingent will need the pace to be genuinely searching to land a blow. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their preferred position; Alfred Tennyson and Little Empire are most likely to actually lock up the spots directly behind Pretty Omagh Girl, with Lohoobb unlikely to get the rear-rank run it wants given the redistribution.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Pretty Omagh Girl dictates an honest but sustainable pace and one of the prominent horses travelling second or third pounces in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Pretty Omagh Girl sets a fair tempo without being burned, and the horse tucked in behind benefits from a perfect cover before unleashing a clean finishing effort on good-to-firm turf that rewards those who conserve energy mid-race; prominent racers get the best of both worlds here — the pace and the clear run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader All The Way
scenarios.trigger: If Pretty Omagh Girl's rivals fail to mount a sustained challenge and she runs through unchallenged to the line.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace rival to burn her, Pretty Omagh Girl simply dictates on her own terms and the prominent horses behind her waste energy jostling for position rather than mounting a coordinated challenge; on ground she handles well, a front-runner allowed an uncontested lead on flat terrain is always capable of making all.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Late Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves stronger than expected and closer types find enough daylight in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Ohailbhic or Exquisite Acclaim would need the leaders to overdo it and the field to open up late, giving them a run through — both are genuine hold-up performers though neither has been firing at the top of their game in similar going recently; this scenario's probability is capped because Lohoobb, the most notable redistributed hold-up type, is unlikely to get a true rear-rank position and its STYLE_FIT discount applies.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Chaos Breaks
scenarios.trigger: If the three prominent types — Alfred Tennyson, Little Empire and Indigo Dream — fight for position aggressively early and the pace fractures.
scenarios.body: A messy early scramble for the prominent slots could unsettle the tempo and create a bunched finish where a fresh-looking hold-up horse finds a gap, but with only 7 runners and a flat track this scenario requires multiple runners to race outside their comfort zone simultaneously; the limited field size makes truly chaotic pace dynamics unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Pretty Omagh Girl's ability to dictate without any pressing pace means she could control the race entirely — if she builds a commanding lead through the first 4f, prominent horses that fail to keep tabs early are at serious risk of being left with too much to do.

Alfred Tennyson and Little Empire both want to be prominent, and with Indigo Dream also racing in that style, watch the first two furlongs for a scrimmage behind Pretty Omagh Girl that could see Chris Hayes' mount knocked sideways or forced wide out of its preferred slot.

Lohoobb returns on just 3 days' rest — the rapid turnaround combined with its redistributed mapping position means W J Lee may struggle to get the horse settled into a rhythm it recognises; watch for signs of over-racing or a snatchy early display.

Ohailbhic is the most interesting hold-up runner given two recent wins at Sligo over 8f — if the pace is stronger than the lone-leader dynamic suggests and the final two furlongs truly open up, Ronan Whelan will be the one looking for a gap from the back.

The Good To Firm going (confirmed across all 7f races on the card) is consistent and fast — any runner with a headgear flag (Alfred Tennyson in tongue-tie, Exquisite Acclaim in visor) bears watching for whether the equipment change produces an early behavioural change at the start or in the first furlong.

races.name: Darley Irish EBF Hurry Harriet Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Hollys Graces
runners_data.note: De Bromhead-trained hold-up specialist returning after 18 days, with solid Good-ground sim-going form (4 from 7 in-the-frame), but the congested front end means she is unlikely to find her natural rear-of-field berth, compromising her chance in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Hollys Graces does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and that second last time out shows she can compete — though an official mark of 85 and a midfield ranking give her plenty to do from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Lemsairbat
runners_data.note: One of two confirmed front-runners here, Joseph O'Brien's five-year-old has been placed six times in 15 similar-ground starts and brings strong recent form including two runner-up finishes; the key question is whether she can withstand Star Performer's challenge for the lead.
runners_data.comment: Lemsaidbat has been knocking on the door, finishing second two starts back and third last time out, and she has experience over today's trip — the main risk is that she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Sun
runners_data.note: Harrington's lightly-raced three-year-old has won once and placed twice from three Good-ground starts, showing a progressive profile, but as a natural closer she will be squeezed forward by the pace-heavy field and may not get the race run to suit.
runners_data.comment: Moonlit Sun won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing consistency, though fourth last time out is a concern; she has run over today's trip and a 97 rating suggests ability, but 127 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Skydance
runners_data.note: A genuine Good-ground performer with seven from seven in-the-frame on similar going, McCreery's three-year-old has the profile to sit mid-division, travel comfortably through a pressured gallop, and sustain her effort over this extra trip — distance is the slight unknown.
runners_data.comment: Skydance franked her winning form with a third last time out, and a winner two starts back, arriving here fit on 18 days' rest with going experience to call on — a thoroughly live contender off 127 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Star Performer
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner (OR 120) and a confirmed front-runner, McDonogh partners a horse whose sole start was a convincing nine-furlong win on Good; she sets the pace dynamic for the whole race and must be respected as the primary pace-setter.
runners_data.comment: Star Performer won last time out, which counts in her favour, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but ranked last of eight on our figures and carrying 127 lb, she faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals here.

runners_data.name: Subsonic
runners_data.note: Murtagh's four-year-old wears a tongue-strap and has Good-ground placed form but has been out of the frame in her last four runs, needing a strongly-run pace to bring out her best — her one win came on Soft and the step up in class is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Subsonic shaped well for a third three starts back and scored four starts back, showing she retains ability at this trip and going; the risk is that two below-par efforts in her most recent outings leave fitness and consistency to prove.

runners_data.name: Classiest
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's prominent-style three-year-old makes her return after 289 days off the track — she won on her sole start at Leopardstown — and while the long layoff demands caution, Whelan takes the ride and the prominent style suits this race shape well.
runners_data.comment: A long absence of 289 days is the chief concern here, and her rating ranks her near the foot of the field; that sole recent start did end in victory, however, giving her something to build on if fitness holds.

runners_data.name: Minerva
runners_data.note: The second A P O'Brien runner, Lordan aboard, brings credible form across seven and eight-furlong races on Good and Yielding, and the prominent style fits naturally into what this pace scenario creates; the step up to 1m1½f is a question but the form reads well enough to be respected.
runners_data.comment: Minerva was a winner two starts back and third three starts back, and has run over this trip before; the chief concern is a 109-day absence, though she has plenty to offer if returning to peak condition.

races.paceDynamic: Star Performer and Lemsairbat are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off, creating a genuine, honest gallop over this 1m1½f trip on Good to Firm ground — neither is likely to surrender without a fight, meaning the pace will be true rather than manufactured. Classiest and Minerva will look to press from prominent positions, adding further pressure to the front end and ensuring the tempo is sustained throughout. Skydance and Subsonic will track from midfield or just off the pace, with Hollys Graces and Moonlit Sun — both natural hold-up horses — unable to settle as deep as they would prefer given the field's overall forward bias; the field holds more hold-up types than can all secure a genuine rear position, and Hollys Graces and Moonlit Sun are the two most likely to find themselves racing further forward than ideal. This race shape — a truly-run, pressured gallop set by two front-runners — strongly favours hold-up or late-running profiles in theory, but because the genuine closers are compromised by redistribution, the biggest beneficiaries will be the prominent and mid-division horses who can travel sweetly in a sound rhythm and produce a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Star Performer and Lemsairbat fight out a genuine gallop and the race is run at an honest tempo throughout, horses who travel prominently and sustain their effort into the straight benefit most.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a true gallop that strings the field out, burning off the closers who cannot get close enough, and a horse travelling smoothly just off the pace picks them off in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Star Performer, the higher-rated and race-fit front-runner, is allowed a soft lead or dictates a controlled pace, she can prove hard to catch on this good to firm surface.
scenarios.body: Star Performer gets a clear sighting from the front and, if Lemsairbat is unable to match her early stride, she can set her own fractions and quicken clear when asked — her sole run was a convincing nine-furlong win on Good.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce and the front-runners tie each other up, a horse sitting midfield and travelling powerfully through the race can finish off a weakening front rank.
scenarios.body: Skydance has strong Good-ground form and would relish a strongly-run contest that brings stamina into play at this 1m1½f trip, while Subsonic's record shows she can run well when the gallop is genuine.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace is strong enough to create a truly strung-out affair and the supposed closers can find clear running despite their compressed positions, a hold-up type gets home late.
scenarios.body: This is the lowest-probability shape because both Hollys Graces and Moonlit Sun are likely to be pushed out of their natural role by the sheer volume of early pace, reducing the chance they settle deep enough to produce a telling late run.

watchPoints.text: Star Performer and Lemsairbat — watch whether they genuinely fight for the lead from the gate or if one concedes, as this single factor determines the pace of the entire race.
Classiest — monitor her keenness and freshness in the first two furlongs given 289 days off the track; a flighty, hard-pulling prominent runner in a fast-pace race can burn out.
Moonlit Sun and Hollys Graces — watch their early positioning; if both are forced to race further forward than their natural style demands, their finishing kicks in the straight will be blunted.
Skydance — watch her position at halfway; if she is travelling comfortably in mid-division through a truly run gallop, she becomes a potent late threat given her unbeaten Good-ground record.
Subsonic — watch for the tongue-strap effect and whether she settles in the early stages; if she is scrubbed along before halfway she is unlikely to raise a serious challenge at Listed level.

races.name: McEnery Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner at OR 100 and top weight, posting decent each-way form at this trip including a second and third at 14f on Good; the 53-day absence is a slight query but trainer Robson De Aguiar has had limited recent winners, and Dallas Star's main role here may be burning out rivals rather than winning.
runners_data.comment: Dallas Star heads this 11-runner field on our ratings, and his best recent form — a second four starts back and thirds five and six starts back — underlines his place-finding consistency. Winless in his last six, though, and a return from 53 days off needs monitoring.

runners_data.name: Fixation
runners_data.note: Returned to form when winning over 10f on Good recently and placed twice at 8f; Ben Coen is a major positive, but stepping up to 1m4½f for the first time is a significant stamina test and the headgear flag warrants monitoring given recent inconsistency.
runners_data.comment: Fixation won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, arriving fit on a 12-day turnaround carrying 130 lb — the main concern is that unplaced effort last time out, which must be forgiven if he's to land this.

runners_data.name: Royal Hollow
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up horse with a string of placed efforts at 13-16f on Good ground, making this trip and surface a natural fit; trainer-jockey combination Andrew Slattery holds the reins on both sides, and the horse's ability to finish reliably is its primary weapon in a strongly-run race.
runners_data.comment: Royal Hollow showed smart form when second two starts back, but her latest sixth is harder to ignore; she has run over today's trip and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround, though rated 90 she faces a stiff task from seventh in the rankings.

runners_data.name: Marazion
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Good and placed over 14f, giving confidence over the trip; Shane Foley takes over from the saddle and the horse's front-running style could prove costly if locked in a battle with Dallas Star and Ephesus, though if it breaks cleanly it may be the classiest of the pace-setters.
runners_data.comment: Marazion shapes as a each-way contender on her best form — a winner four starts back and a second three starts back — but consecutive sixths in recent starts raise a question mark, and 45 days off the track adds a fitness query despite experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: War Rooms
runners_data.note: Won last time at 13f on Good and drops back to a prominent hold-up role naturally; Colin Keane, the booking of the day, knows how to position a hold-up horse in a truly-run contest, and recent good-ground form makes this a strong profile fit for a pace-heavy scenario.
runners_data.comment: War Rooms brings a recent win to the table and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, while carrying 129 lb looks manageable for a gelding our ratings rank as a leading contender — the main risk is that his form outside that victory has been patchy.

runners_data.name: Obscenity
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 12f on Good and placed consistently in similar company; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a top-tier booking and the horse's prominent-tracking style suits a race where the front-runners empty themselves — the visored headgear suggests a horse that needs to be kept mentally focused.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out after two wins in his last five starts, Obscenity arrives 45 days later needing to bounce back sharply; rated well below the top of the market on our figures, he's a hard sell despite having run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Star Harbour
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old carrying headgear (visors) and consistent in 12f Good-ground handicaps, placing at 11f recently; lacks a recent win over this longer trip but its proximity finishes suggest it won't be far away if the race is run to suit prominent trackers, though OR 86 may prove its ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Star Harbour shaped with promise when runner-up three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going underpins a strong threat at 126 lb — the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Navy Waters
runners_data.note: Placed at 14f and 16f on Good ground with two course-distance wins in similar conditions, making this trip a known quantity; carries visors, has been freshened up on 12 days' turnaround, and a prominent racing style should allow it to remain competitive without being sucked into the early pace battle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Navy Waters does bring distance experience and a fitness edge fresh from a run 12 days ago, but her recent string of fifth-fourth-fifth finishes suggests she finds one or two too good, and the 125 lb burden won't help her cause here.

runners_data.name: Daboya
runners_data.note: Has won twice recently at 12-13f on Good ground and is lightly weighted at OR 80 with an apprentice claiming 7lbs; Daboya's natural instinct is to race prominently, but with Dallas Star, Marazion, and Ephesus dominating the front positions, it is likely to be pushed back and forced to race out of its preferred role, which meaningfully tempers its chance.
runners_data.comment: Daboya has back-to-back wins in her recent starts, but our figures rank her last of eleven here and she faces a stiff ask stepping up in class. Has run over today's trip, at least, and arrives fresh after 36 days off.

runners_data.name: Sea Coral
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has placed three times in a row over 12-13f on Good ground and runs freshly with cheekpieces, suggesting connections are looking to sharpen her up; the longer 1m4½f trip is a slight unknown but the pace dynamics here set up well for a strong late finisher if she can quicken sufficiently.
runners_data.comment: Placed third in each of her last two starts, Sea Coral arrives 23 days fresh and has run over today's trip and going before, but she remains winless in her last five and her ranking of eighth from eleven suggests only a midfield share of the spoils.

runners_data.name: Ephesus
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner at the bottom of the weights and ridden by a 10lb claimer, with form figures of 100-98 suggesting erratic reliability; Ephesus's role is more likely that of pace-contributor than winner, and its recent history of finishing 7th-11th in sprints up to 20f on Good raises serious stamina and class questions at this level.
runners_data.comment: Ephesus has tumbled down the placings in his last four starts after winning, and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, he is hard to fancy here. He has run over today's trip and going before, and his 11-day turnaround at least suggests fitness.

races.paceDynamic: Dallas Star, Marazion, and Ephesus are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a strong early gallop over 1m4½f on Good to Firm ground at Gowran, with each likely to contest the lead from the outset and stretch the field through the first half of the race. The pace battle between these three will almost certainly produce a truly-run contest, putting stamina at a premium and making any attempt to dictate from the front an energy-sapping proposition. With the gallop set to be honest throughout, hold-up and midfield runners who can conserve energy behind a genuine pace and finish strongly — War Rooms, Royal Hollow, and Sea Coral in particular — are the profiles this race shape most clearly favours. The field contains more front-running and prominent types than can comfortably hold their natural positions; Daboya, a genuine prominent racer, has been redistributed to midfield because Dallas Star, Marazion, and Ephesus will take that space, meaning Daboya is unlikely to secure its preferred berth and its chance in a prominent-led shape must be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Dallas Star, Marazion, and Ephesus fight for the lead and sustain a strong gallop throughout, burning each other out before the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners press each other relentlessly, leaving the field strung out and exhausted at the head of affairs, setting the race up perfectly for a strong finisher coming from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace-Setter Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most likely Marazion or Dallas Star — quickly asserts and the others accept a secondary position, producing a controlled yet honest gallop.
scenarios.body: A single horse dictates at a sustainable pace, removing the worst of the energy-sapping battle up front, and the race becomes a test of class and course-suitability in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fractures in the middle stages and a prominent-tracking horse such as Obscenity or Star Harbour sits just off the leader and pounces two out.
scenarios.body: The front three begin to weaken from their exertions in the latter stages while a horse that travelled prominently but avoided the pace battle cruises past into contention.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so fierce that the field comes back dramatically to a hold-up horse producing a strong, sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Royal Hollow or War Rooms, given extra time to switch and build momentum, accelerates past the weakening pack in the final furlong on the Good to Firm surface that suits both.

watchPoints.text: Dallas Star, Marazion, and Ephesus will all contest the lead from the start — watch for a contested breakaway in the opening quarter-mile that could set a punishing gallop and compromise each other's finishing chances entirely.

War Rooms is ridden by Colin Keane and won last time at 13f on Good; in a truly-run race this profile is at maximum danger, and Keane's positioning in the first half-mile will be the key tell for how seriously to take the hold-up case.

Daboya has been pushed out of its natural prominent position by the strength of pace in this field — watch whether Reese Holohan (7lb claimer) attempts to force it forward regardless, which could lead to a costly change of tactics and energy expenditure.

Obscenity's last run was a well-beaten 12th on Good at 12f, which is a notable form reversal from its earlier wins — watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle elects to track the pace closely or drops in, as the horse's visor suggests it may be unsettled by crowd noise or traffic early.

Sea Coral steps up in distance to 1m4½f wearing cheekpieces for the first time — a market move on the strength of conditions and expected pace will be informative, as connections appear to be engineering a set-up race.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden

runners_data.name: Believe Again
runners_data.note: A five-year-old hold-up performer for Seamus O'Donnell whose recent form reads two zeros, and who fades in the finish; mapped to midfield as the field is saturated with hold-up types, meaning she is unlikely to operate from her preferred position, further compromising an already modest profile.

runners_data.name: Highlander Addict
runners_data.note: Best form over 13-17f in good ground — Patrick Flynn's five-year-old has genuine class (1 win, 3 places in similar conditions) but drops sharply in trip here, making this distance a real question mark even though the going suits; Alan Persse (5lb claimer) adds weight considerations.

runners_data.name: Lonelyharbourwall
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's lightly-raced four-year-old has only one run on record — a distant 10th on soft over 2m — and her unknown style and uncertainty around both going and trip make her deeply hard to assess; Chris Hayes retains the ride but lightly-raced tag and fading tendency demand caution.

runners_data.name: Gliondar
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old shaped encouragingly when runner-up on good ground over 8f, and the step up to 1m1½f looks well-judged; Dylan Browne McMonagle is among Ireland's very best and will likely slot into the perfect tracking position behind Jumpingthegun from an early stage.

runners_data.name: Jumpingthegun
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's three-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner in the race and Rory Cleary can dictate terms completely; form of 7-4-3 on varied surfaces shows modest ability but his positional advantage is the key factor and he could prove very hard to catch if allowed a soft lead.

runners_data.name: Blue Orquidea
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's three-year-old is a natural hold-up horse whose two runs have returned a 13th and a 5th — she has been placed in midfield on the map because the field is too back-heavy to accommodate her at the rear, meaning she faces the double disadvantage of an unfamiliar position and a short 0W0P record on this going.

runners_data.name: Salamina
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's unraced three-year-old is a complete unknown — no style classification, no going verdict, no form — but the trainer's strike rate of 7/66 in 14 days and Colin Keane's absence (Declan McDonogh takes the ride) suggests measured expectations rather than a stable confidence play; breeding and stable profile are the only positives.

runners_data.name: Socratea
runners_data.note: McCreery's three-year-old hold-up horse has one run to her name — a 7th on good over 8f — and Ronan Whelan takes the ride; the step up to 1m1½f on firmer ground could suit a horse who appeared to be staying on late, but sample size is too small to lean heavily on.

runners_data.name: Storm Petrel
runners_data.note: Has shown progressive form over 7-9f on good ground with a third placing at 9f for Ms M McDowall; a natural hold-up horse placed in midfield due to the volume of back-runners in this field, and the style-fit discount applies — Gary Halpin will need to improvise positionally in a way that may not flatter the horse's true ability.

runners_data.name: Xirivella
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's three-year-old has two runs on good ground returning a 3rd and a 6th, both over 8f — Colin Keane takes the ride and the distance step looks positive for a horse who was staying on; a prominent racer who should secure her natural position and represents a live each-way interest in the tracking scenario.

runners_data.name: Karrygrant
runners_data.note: John Murtagh's three-year-old has consistent form (3-2-4-5-2-3 in recent runs) and Ben Coen rides — placed on both good and soft ground, the step to 1m1½f is the question given all form is over 8-10f; prominent style suits the projected race shape and he brings more experience than most rivals.

runners_data.name: Lord Darragh
runners_data.note: Rory Devine's lightly-raced three-year-old finished 6th on good ground over 8f for Luke McAteer — hold-up style in a field of hold-up horses means he is unlikely to travel in the position he ideally needs, and the absence of any recent evidence of staying ability makes this a speculative runner at this distance.

runners_data.name: One Cool County
runners_data.note: P J Murphy's three-year-old was 6th over 12f on good ground, suggesting the trip is not beyond him, but a 7lb claimer (Conor Cusack) in a 15-runner field is a notable negative; a natural hold-up runner in a crowded rear section, he needs a great deal to go right.

runners_data.name: Rock Of Claremont
runners_data.note: Aidan Oliver's three-year-old has form of 5th and 3rd on standard and good ground over 8f — W J Lee takes the ride and prominent style puts him in the ideal position to track the pace; the trip extension is the key question but placed form suggests enough ability to compete if the race unfolds at a moderate tempo.

runners_data.name: Yogini
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's three-year-old was runner-up over 12f on good ground and has form over staying distances — Gavin Ryan rides, and if this 1m1½f trip is a stepping stone back in trip after longer runs, she could bring untapped reserves late; tongue-tie and breast-girth headgear hint at a trainer looking to unlock more.

races.paceDynamic: Jumpingthegun is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him, is set to control matters from the front at a tempo of his own choosing on good-to-firm ground over 1m1½f at Gowran. The prominent types Gliondar, Xirivella, Karrygrant, and Rock Of Claremont will contest the positions just behind him, creating a compact lead group but not a truly contested pace — meaning the fractions are unlikely to be punishing. With Jumpingthegun able to dictate a sustainable gallop, the race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can conserve energy and produce a meaningful sustained finish, provided the pace is honest enough to set them up — but if the pace is soft, prominent closers who track just off the leader without expending energy will be ideally placed. Note that Blue Orquidea, Believe Again, and Storm Petrel are genuine hold-up horses shown in midfield on the map because the field contains more natural hold-up types than can all be accommodated at the rear; Gliondar and Xirivella are the prominent runners most likely to secure their natural positions given jockey quality and draw. The tactical verdict favours the prominent-to-midfield profile: horses who can track the uncontested Jumpingthegun within two or three lengths and strike when the pace steadies approaching the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jumpingthegun Leads, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Jumpingthegun dictates an uncontested, moderate tempo and the race is decided by those travelling smoothly in the slipstream.
scenarios.body: Jumpingthegun sets fractions that are comfortable for prominent horses just behind, and when he has nothing left in the tank entering the final quarter-mile the tracking riders pounce with decisive, well-timed runs; the good-to-firm ground rewards horses with a clean, efficient action who save every ounce racing off the pace. Gliondar, trained by Joseph O'Brien and ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle, is ideally suited tracking the lone front-runner, while Xirivella (Colin Keane, Noel Meade) and Karrygrant (Ben Coen) hold prominent positions without being over-extended.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Ups Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Jumpingthegun sets a truly dawdling gallop and the prominent horses get into a sprint finish too early, leaving the back-markers with ground to make up but a clear run.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace paradoxically helps genuine hold-up horses if those in front get into a tussle or run out of steam sharply inside the final furlong, opening a gap for late runners to motor through on fast ground; Highlander Addict, who has placed over longer trips in good ground, is the archetype here, while Socratea could pick up late if given a clear passage. Believe Again and Storm Petrel are true hold-up types racing from mid-pack rather than their natural position, tempering confidence in either delivering their best effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jumpingthegun Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Jumpingthegun gets away cleanly, is allowed a soft lead throughout, and the prominent horses are too slow to recognise the threat and react in time.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to apply early pressure, Jumpingthegun could build an unassailable advantage by the time jockeys behind him wake to the danger, and a modest OR of 80 becomes irrelevant if the race is run to suit his strengths; the Gordon Elliott yard has the talent to prime a lightly-campaigned horse for precisely this kind of tactical race, and Rory Cleary has the experience to manage the tempo intelligently. This scenario punishes the hold-up horses most severely and rewards Jumpingthegun's positional advantage outright.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Open Finish, Class Resolves
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and the race becomes an all-out test of class and stamina in the closing stages with multiple horses in contention.
scenarios.body: A competitive finish across a broad front on good-to-firm ground brings the highest-rated, best-credentialled horses to the fore regardless of style, with Joseph O'Brien's Salamina — a debutante with serious breeding potential — capable of producing an eye-catching run if forward enough; Yogini, who shaped with ability when runner-up over 12f on good ground, could also be competitive if this distance and going combination draws out improvement. Blue Orquidea is racing out of her natural hold-up role and the style-fit discount applies, limiting confidence that she delivers here.

watchPoints.text: Watch Jumpingthegun's early splits — if Rory Cleary is allowed to build a soft lead unchallenged through the first half-mile, the race could be over before the prominent brigade realise the danger.

Gliondar and Xirivella will both want to track the leader from early — monitor how cleanly Dylan Browne McMonagle and Colin Keane establish their positions in the first furlong in a 15-runner field where minor scrimmaging could cost lengths.

Blue Orquidea, Believe Again, and Storm Petrel are all genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield by the weight of similar types in this field — if any of them are checked or lose momentum mid-race, their already-compromised chances are effectively ended.

Salamina debuts for Joseph O'Brien under Declan McDonogh rather than a top-level booking — watch her market move in the minutes before post time as a guide to stable confidence, given zero public form to assess.

Karrygrant's headgear (p — first time?) and Yogini's tongue-tie/breast-girth combination are worth monitoring at the start to confirm headgear is applied correctly and both horses break cleanly, as either could be unsettled if not.

races.name: 1XBET IRISH SPIRIT Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: She's Ideal
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's 4yo has a 1W2P record on similar going from 14 runs, sits in the prominent position naturally, and rates the most dangerous stalker in a race where tracking Pimlico Piranha from second or third is the golden ticket; 23 days since last run is no concern.
runners_data.comment: She's Ideal bounced back to winning ways last time out and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions hold no fears; drawn in stall four carrying 142 lb, she looks the one to follow on current form despite a patchy middle spell.

runners_data.name: Keilah
runners_data.note: 6yo hold-up mare whose 13/15 sim-going record suggests she handles the surface but has predominantly raced over 18f of late — this 9.5f trip is shorter than her preferred range and the hold-up style leaves her dependent on a pace she is unlikely to get today.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Keilah nonetheless showed clear ability with a second three starts back and a third four starts back — her experience over today's trip and going keeps her firmly in contention, though that seventh last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: Consistent H-style runner but a 15-8 sim-going record with zero wins is a red flag; all five recent runs have been over 8f and she steps up in trip today, making a prominent enough position to offset the hold-up style difficult to envisage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Perfect Judgement nonetheless tops our ratings in a field of 20 and carries a strong fitness edge at 21 days — he has run over today's trip and draws stall one; the chief risk is that recent form, including an unplaced effort last time, leaves him with plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's 4yo is a natural prominent racer returning on just 8 days' rest, which for a lightly-raced handicapper can signal the yard has it spot-right; 0W2P on good going is modest but the prominent tag suits this race shape perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a third four starts back the sole bright spot in a sequence that includes sevenths last time out and three starts back; he carries 138 lb from stall 14 and a trainer in a cold spell of 0/21 makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Giselles Defence
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Sean Davis which often indicates a straightforward intended ride; the hold-up style and a sim-going record of 8/15 with one win suggest occasional sparks but the 23d break and a non-threatening OR=53 limit expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Giselles Defence at least has experience over today's trip and going, and a 23-day break could help; carrying 135 lb from stall 12, though, he faces a stiff task off an official mark of 53.

runners_data.name: Thompson Gunner
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on standard Tapeta in good style but his four AW runs make his turf form on good ground a genuine unknown — sim-going shows only 4/15 0W0P, and being forced into midfield rather than his natural hold-up berth further complicates matters after 145 days off.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back but unplaced last time out, and 145 days on the sidelines makes Thompson Gunner a fitness query returning here; he has run over today's trip and a rating of 63 offers some encouragement, though the layoff is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Pimlico Piranha
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who gets to bowl along unchallenged, but a form string of 9-8-10 with a fade flag is a serious concern — he is the race's pace-maker not its winner, and the 47-day break has not obviously freshened a horse that has yet to threaten.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts — all unplaced — Pimlico Piranha has done little to inspire confidence, and our figures rank him well down the field; 47 days off adds a fitness query, though he has the experience of recent starts to draw on.

runners_data.name: Tullyesker
runners_data.note: 4yo whose four career runs show only going into single figures on good ground once; the fade flag and forced midfield position (a natural hold-up type squeezed out by numbers) combine to make this a very tough ask at 42 days off.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a pair of eighths and two unplaced efforts, Tullyesker arrives 42 days freshened up and has run over today's trip — but rated just 43 officially and ranked 15th of 20 on our figures, he is hard to fancy on current form.

runners_data.name: Gold Dublooms
runners_data.note: OR=40 is the joint-lowest in the race and a form line reading 5-0-9-0-0 gives little encouragement; the hold-up style is its natural preference but being mapped to midfield because of field size removes even that limited edge, with a fade warning compounding the negatives.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with three unplaced efforts in his most recent three runs, Gold Dublooms is hard to fancy here; he has run over today's trip and returns after 32 days, but his official rating of 40 tells its own story.

runners_data.name: Connova
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes takes the ride on this lightly-raced 3yo whose last three runs all produced top-4 finishes over 10f on good ground — the most consistent recent form in the hold-up group, and while pushed slightly forward of its natural position, the proximity to the pace could suit if the race quickens late.
runners_data.comment: Connova has shown admirable consistency in her last three starts, finishing third twice and fourth once, and has run over today's trip — the main concern is that she remains yet to win in recent starts despite that placed form.

runners_data.name: Georg Zhukov
runners_data.note: OR=53 turf headgear runner whose last win came over 10f on good ground at Eamonn O'Connell's yard; naturally a hold-up horse finding itself mapped to midfield in a field overloaded with closers, meaning its best chance rests on the traffic clearing rather than any positional advantage.

runners_data.name: Pettus Bridge
runners_data.note: Reserve 2 jockey on a 4yo that has finished 9th-9th-11th in its three career starts, all on good going; the prominent style gives it a structural edge over most of its rivals today, though the consistent low finishes suggest the level is the limiting factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with back-to-back ninth-place finishes and an unplaced effort before that, Pettus Bridge faces a stiff ask from stall 13 carrying 130 lb, and our rating of 37 leaves him well held on these figures.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: 6yo veteran with zero wins or places across 15 qualifying runs on similar going; forced into midfield from a natural hold-up preference, and a fade flag on top of that profile makes this a very difficult horse to back into any argument.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts with a sequence littered with unplaced efforts, Bang Po is hard to fancy on these figures, ranked 17 of 20; 41 days off the track doesn't obviously help, though he has run over today's trip before and carries a manageable 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Omissions
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes a high-profile booking on this 3yo, but three runs all ending 9th or worse with a fade flag is discouraging; the hold-up style leaves it reliant on a truly strong pace that simply is not expected here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a pair of ninths and an unplaced effort telling a grim story, Omissions is ranked last on our figures and faces a stiff task here — though 28 days between runs at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: No More Hiding
runners_data.note: A Oliver yard's 3yo has only one qualifying run on good going from six starts and that produced an 8th; 59 days since last run is a long layoff and the fade warning on a horse that needs a pace it is unlikely to encounter is a compounding concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and quiet for 59 days, No More Hiding faces a stiff ask from stall nine carrying 130 lb, yet is rated 11th of these and has a speed rating of 63.

runners_data.name: Shelbourne Flyer
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's 5yo has 0W2P from nine qualifying runs and its best recent result was a 6th over 7f — today's 9.5f is a stretch for a horse whose body of work suggests it rarely threatens; the natural hold-up style pushed to midfield compounds an already difficult task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn in stall 16 carrying 130 lb, Shelbourne Flyer faces an uphill task, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a manageable 23-day break; a trainer strike-rate of just 4% in the last fortnight is a further dampener.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: Six consecutive zeros from 2021 onwards tell a stark story; sim-going record of 10/15 0W1P on good and a fade tag leave this 6yo with almost no route to relevance regardless of race shape, and the E D Delany yard is not in notable form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Lohengrin arrives 21 days fresh with experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, yet a ranking of 12th of 20 on our ratings and an official mark of 47 suggest he faces a stiff task from stall 3 carrying 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Karl Thornton's 3yo posted a 4th over 10f on good last time and has placed twice in five good-ground tries — by the standards of the hold-up cohort that is reasonable; Ben Coen's booking adds interest and the trip suits, though the style still leaves it dependent on late gaps appearing.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Onyeisi does at least have experience over today's trip and comes here on a handy 26-day break, but a fourth being his best recent effort and carrying 129 lb from stall 18 leaves him with plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Cameclose
runners_data.note: James Ryan takes the ride but three finishes of 9th or worse in its last three starts on good ground outweigh the 2nd on a previous visit — the fade flag is prominent, and this naturally hold-up type is unlikely to get the position or the pace scenario it needs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Cameclose does bring a second last time out and has run over today's trip, though a couple of ninths in between suggest inconsistency; the 51-day break and a mark of 53 leave questions from stall two.

runners_data.name: La Campanella
runners_data.note: Colin Keane on board gives the race its most notable jockey-horse mismatch in terms of market expectation versus form — OR=45 with 0W0P in nine qualifying runs and a fade flag; the turf-plus-pace headgear profile has not unlocked anything so far, and midfield is not where it wants to be.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and drawn 19, La Campanella faces an uphill task, though she has run over today's trip before and a return after 42 days could see her sharper; a fourth last time out is at least a step in the right direction.

races.paceDynamic: Pimlico Piranha is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 20-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to pressurise them — She's Ideal and William F Browne are prominent types who will sit behind rather than challenge for the lead, meaning Pimlico Piranha can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout the 1m1½f trip on Good to Firm ground. With only one horse setting fractions, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, creating a race that plays into the hands of those who can track the leader in the first three or four and produce a finish from a position of proximity. The field is saturated with hold-up horses — Georg Zhukov, Cameclose, Thompson Gunner, Connova, Shelbourne Flyer and Bang Po among many others — far more than can realistically settle at the rear, meaning several will be forced wider and higher in the order than they would naturally prefer, reducing the late-run threat from that cohort. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can travel just off Pimlico Piranha's steady tempo and kick from two furlongs out hold the structural advantage; closers face a true-pace deficit and a crowded route through traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Pimlico Piranha bowls along at a comfortable clip and She's Ideal or William F Browne track in second or third throughout.
scenarios.body: The moderate, uncontested gallop set by Pimlico Piranha hands the race to those who can sit just off the pace in clean air and attack from two out; She's Ideal and William F Browne are the best-placed prominent types to pounce as the leader fades on the quick ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Trio Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Pimlico Piranha goes even slower than expected and the race becomes a false-pace procession with no one willing to challenge.
scenarios.body: A dawdle suits the handful of horses in the first four lengths who have enough finishing pace to sprint clear from the final quarter-mile; She's Ideal's sim-going form and Connova's consistent top-three finishes on good ground make them dangerous in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If a true closer manages to secure a better position than the redistribution suggests and the pace quickens sufficiently off the home turn to create a gap.
scenarios.body: Georg Zhukov's OR=53 and turf headgear flag some residual each-way appeal if traffic clears on the turn, while Onyeisi's recent 4th over course-relevant 10f on good gives it a slim squeak; both need a wall of horses in front to collapse on cue.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large 20-runner field produces significant trouble in running at the tight home turn and the race fragments into multiple groups.
scenarios.body: Shelbourne Flyer and La Campanella are at the longer end of the market with profiles that could theoretically benefit from wholesale interference bunching the field, gifting them an unobstructed passage; both are out-of-role hold-up types whose chances otherwise look slim.

watchPoints.text: Pimlico Piranha sets the entire pace for a 20-runner field yet carries a fade flag and has finished 9th-8th-10th in all three career starts — if it is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and then weakens sharply inside the final two furlongs, the race could collapse in a heap for those tracking in second and third.

She's Ideal and William F Browne are both prominent types who will likely contest positions two and three behind Pimlico Piranha; watch the early stages to see who secures the cleaner, shorter route on the rail, as the horse that achieves that in a 20-runner field on a tight track shapes as the one with the decisive tactical edge.

The sheer volume of redistributed hold-up horses — Georg Zhukov, Cameclose, Thompson Gunner, Connova, Shelbourne Flyer and others — means the home turn at Gowran with a full field of 20 is a significant trouble-in-running risk; any horse drawn wide and forced to go around runners at that point is likely to surrender its chance.

Connova's jockey Chris Hayes is the standout booking among the hold-up group and its last three runs have all been top-4 finishes over the same 10f trip on good ground; if it manages to find a position closer to prominent than its natural style suggests, it becomes an unexposed each-way factor worth monitoring.

Dylan Browne McMonagle's ride on Omissions is the highest-profile booking in the race by reputation — watch whether he attempts to overcome the hold-up profile by positioning closer than the horse has historically raced, as any such tactical adjustment in a moderate-pace race would be a significant red flag for the prominent stalkers.
